Subject: INTERNAL: Urgent — Finnova requires SOC2 Type II + bridge letter by Thu EOD to proceed (DEAL-78912)

Team — quick escalation. Finnova (prospect) sent a formal request for our SOC 2 Type II and asked specifically for a bridge letter covering any post-audit control changes. Procurement needs confirmation by end of day Thursday to keep the pilot start date.

Why urgent: we already have commercial momentum; if we miss this window they’ve signaled they’ll pause.

What I need from security/compliance:
1) Confirm current SOC 2 Type II audit period and whether it covers controls through our intended pilot go-live (tentative 2026-07-22).
2) Can we issue a bridge letter / interim attestation that will satisfy Finnova’s procurement? If yes, what is the turnaround (hours/days) and what signoffs are required?
3) List of evidence artifacts you need to assemble immediately.

Marissa — this is high-priority for the deal team. Rishi / Neha, can we treat this as an expedited sprint?

Thanks,
Dylan

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-10T17:00:00Z
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Urgent — Finnova requires SOC2 Type II + bridge letter by Thu EOD to proceed (DEAL-78912)

Thanks for the ping. Quick status: our latest SOC 2 Type II report covers the period 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31 and was issued by KPMG. That means the formal attestation does not cover events after 2025-12-31 (notably a control migration we completed on 2026-02-10).

We can provide a bridge letter that documents the change and provides management assertions about the control state post-audit. Typical steps:
- Draft bridge letter (internal review) — 1 business day
- Legal + external auditor acknowledgment/signoff (if required) — 2–4 business days
- Evidence bundle for procurement (logs, runbooks, config exports) — depends on artifacts but we can assemble a preliminary set within 24 hours if we prioritize

Constraints: the external auditor (KPMG) is not required for every bridge letter, but some customers demand auditor acknowledgment which adds time. We need clarity from Finnova on whether an internal bridge letter (management assertion) is acceptable or if they need auditor confirmation.

Neha — can you stand up an evidence manifest and draft the bridge letter template this evening? I can review and route to legal. If Marissa and Dylan authorize a customer-facing sprint (even over the weekend), we can likely meet the Thu EOD ask for a management bridge letter.

-Rishi
Director, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
